case_title: Om Prakash v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (the defence alleged enmity, with one accused alleged to be suspected by the victim of spreading news of her abortion; no relationship between accused and victim is described)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.376(2)(g) (rape, as charged under s.376 against two accused); IPC s.109 read with s.107 (abetment of rape, against third accused)
evidence_type: Eyewitness (victim's testimony), corroborative testimony of mother, medical examination, radiological age determination, school certificate
aggravating_circumstances: Victim was about 15 (minor); victim was kept in the house for about an hour; victim was threatened with elimination if she disclosed the incident; offence committed by two accused acting together
trial_court_outcome: Om Prakash and Kartar Singh convicted under s.376(2)(g) IPC, 10 years RI and Rs.10,000 fine each; Chhoti convicted under s.109 IPC, 3 years RI and Rs.10,000 fine
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence of all three accused affirmed (judgment dated 30.7.2008)
offence_finally_established: Rape under s.376(2)(g) IPC (Om Prakash and Kartar Singh); abetment of rape under s.109 IPC (Chhoti)
neutral_facts: On the day of the incident, the victim, aged about fifteen, was alone at home. The victim's mother was away at another village and other family members were not present. One accused came to the house and asked the victim to fetch lassi from the house of another accused and that accused's spouse. When the victim entered that house, two other men already there bolted the door from inside and raped the victim. The victim was held for about an hour and threatened with elimination if the incident was disclosed. The victim did not disclose the incident for about twenty days, until the mother returned from a maternal visit. The victim then told the mother, and the father took the victim to lodge a report at the police station. The report was registered the next day. The investigating officer inspected the spot and recorded the victim's statement before a magistrate under section 164. A medical examination found no external injuries, no injury to the perineum or thighs, and a healed ruptured hymen that admitted one finger easily. A radiological examination assessed the age as between 14 and 16 years. A school certificate recorded a date of birth showing the victim was fifteen at the time. The victim's testimony and the mother's corroborating account of the delayed disclosure were presented.
physical_harm: No external injuries; no injury over perineum or thighs; hymen of healed ruptured type admitting one finger easily; sexual assault confirmed medically
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.376 and s.109 as framed at trial); 2 finally upheld (s.376(2)(g) and s.109)
premeditation_planning: Not stated (the victim was lured to the house on the pretext of fetching lassi; the court did not make an express finding of premeditation)
key_evidence_accepted: Victim's testimony (PW5) and mother's corroborating statement (PW6) on delayed disclosure; radiological age report (PW2); school certificate (PW11) showing date of birth; medical report (PW9); finding that the victim's consent was immaterial due to age
witness_credibility: Victim's and mother's testimony found natural and trustworthy despite lengthy cross-examination; no false implication due to enmity
post_offence_conduct: Accused threatened the victim not to disclose the incident; victim did not disclose for about 20 days
bail_history: Granted bail by Supreme Court: Chhoti on 18.5.2009; Kartar Singh on 20.7.2009; Om Prakash on 16.4.2010. No other bail history stated
trial_duration: offence: not given (victim disclosed the incident to her mother on 12.6.1995, FIR registered 13.6.1995); trial judgment: 16.12.1996; High Court: 30.7.2008; Supreme Court: 14.10.2014
legal_representation: Accused/appellants: Rishi Malhotra and Prem Malhotra. State/respondent: Nupur Chaudhary, Vivekta Singh and Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: FIR registered 13.6.1995; spot inspected; victim's statement recorded under s.164 CrPC; medical and radiological examinations done; charge-sheet filed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted (the 20-day delay in lodging the FIR was held to be sufficiently explained)
appeal_history: Trial court (Additional Sessions Judge, Hissar, 16.12.1996): all three convicted and sentenced. High Court (30.7.2008): appeal dismissed. Supreme Court: all three appeals dismissed
prosecution_argument: Not stated (the State's submissions are not separately summarised; the Court relied on the trial record and evidence)
defence_argument: Chhoti, being a woman, cannot be convicted under s.376 r/w s.34 or s.109 IPC; mere failure to protect the victim is not abetment (relying on Kulwant Singh and Priya Patel); sentence should be reduced to period already undergone
legal_principle_applied: Abetment under s.107 IPC (third clause: intentional aiding) read with s.109 IPC; a person who aids at the time of the crime is a principal of the second degree; conviction for abetment requires direct involvement or instigation, which the aiding conduct here satisfied
precedent_relied_upon: Kulwant Singh @ Kulbansh Singh v. State of Bihar (2007) 15 SCC 670 (cited by appellants; referred to); Priya Patel v. State of M.P. (2006) 6 SCC 263 (cited by appellants; referred to); Joseph Kurian v. State of Kerala (1994) 6 SCC 535 (as quoted in Kulwant Singh)
sentencing_rationale: Sentence awarded by the trial court and upheld by the High Court found just and proper; no separate reduction granted
other_sentence_order: Accused directed to be taken into custody forthwith to serve remaining sentence
